title: My 20-Minute AI Lesson Planning Sprint
author: Teaching With Intelligence
summary: Lesson planning can shift from hours of preparation to efficient, AI-supported twenty-minute sprints through structured workflow design and clear prompting. The workflow combines curriculum standards, learning objectives, student context, available resources, and instructional best practices into a coherent lesson plan that AI helps develop systematically. The teacher inputs: content topic, grade level, specific learning objective, student background information, time available, available materials, and any instructional preferences. From these inputs, AI generates: essential questions, core concepts, instructional activities, formative assessments, differentiation strategies, and resource suggestions. The workflow is optimized for speed without sacrificing quality. Rather than waiting for perfect questions, teachers work with AI-generated starting points and refine based on classroom knowledge. The twenty-minute sprint includes: five minutes to define scope and objectives, ten minutes of AI-assisted planning with refinement, and five minutes to create backup activities and prepare materials. This differs fundamentally from free-form AI use: the structure, clear inputs, and defined outputs keep the planning productive. Teachers report the sprint format reduces cognitive load (less overwhelm from blank page) while improving quality (more systematic thinking about objectives and differentiation). The workflow emphasizes that AI enhances teacher planning rather than replacing professional judgment. Teachers make final decisions about appropriateness, adjust activities for their specific students, and account for classroom dynamics that AI cannot see. The structured AI assistance handles the mechanical parts of planning—gathering ideas, organizing frameworks, finding activities—freeing teacher expertise for what matters: judgment about student needs, appropriate pacing, meaningful differentiation, and motivating instruction. The technique scales to different grade levels and subject areas through adjusting the AI prompts and inputs.
points: Twenty-minute sprint format reduces planning time while improving systematic thinking
Clear input structure (topic, objectives, student context) makes AI suggestions relevant
Teacher judgment remains central: refinement, appropriateness, differentiation decisions
Workflow prevents blank-page overwhelm while ensuring instructionally sound plans
Process scales across grade levels and subjects through prompt customization
